title: Searcher of Hearts! Before Thy Face
description: Searcher of Hearts! Before Thy Face in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 461 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For Freedom from Secret Sin”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sear-cher of hearts! be-fore thy face I all my soul dis-play; And, con-scious of its in-nate arts, En-treat thy strict sur-vey.

lines: Searcher of hearts! before thy face
I all my soul display;
And, conscious of its innate arts,
Entreat thy strict survey.
If, lurking in its inmost folds,
I any sin conceal,
O, let a ray of light divine
The secret guile reveal.
If tinctured with that odious gall
Unknowing I remain,
Let grace, like a pure silver stream,
Wash out the hateful stain.
If, in these fatal fetters bound,
A wretched slave I lie,
Smite off my chains, and wake my soul
To light and liberty.
To humble penitence and prayer
Be gentle pity given;
Speak ample pardon to my heart,
And seal its claim to heaven.

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
